subject: DPA: sunset/handback synchronization & erasure timing
messages:
From: Elena Markovic <elena.markovic@aurumanalytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@aurumanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA questions — erasure timing and sunset handback

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the call earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our legal and ops teams: they want tighter language around the final "sunset/handback" flow — specifically a clear synchronization window between Redwood triggering a customer account termination and the start of irreversible erasure (including backups). They also asked for an explicit certification we can accept once the erase completes.

Attached our proposed wording (DPA_Aurum_Redlines_v3.docx) — main asks: 1) no less than 14 days notice for final export prior to irreversible erase for EU accounts, 2) confirmation artifact containing timestamped hashes of deleted datasets, and 3) a defined backup retention carveout (short window to allow emergency restore) with max 30 days encrypted backup tombstone before cryptographic destruction.

Can you confirm Redwood can accept those, or propose operational mitigations we can include in the DPA?

Best,
Elena Markovic
Head of Procurement Ops
Aurum Analytics

[Attachment: DPA_Aurum_Redlines_v3.docx]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Markovic <elena.markovic@aurumanalytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA questions — erasure timing and sunset handback

Elena — thanks for the note and the redlines. Quick summary of what we can and can't accept as-is:

- 14 days export notice: we can accept 14 days for EU production accounts if the customer confirms no outstanding legal holds. For platform-initiated terminations (billing default), we propose a 7-day remediation window then a 14-day export window; we can document the trigger flow.
- Certification artifact (timestamped hashes): we can produce a signed erasure certificate containing deleted object IDs, timestamps, and HMAC hashes. It will be generated after final destruction completes; timing depends on backup processing.
- Backup retention carveout (30 days tombstone): we need to clarify scope — full backups vs incremental snapshots and whether on-disk encrypted snapshots are considered "backups" for this clause. Our ops team prefers a 7–30 day configurable tombstone for on-customer-request recovery, but we recommend 14 days by default for EU accounts to meet both restore and privacy needs.

Looping in Laura and Priyom to propose operational language and an erasure playbook for the DPA that can be referenced as an appendix.

Next steps: Laura/PRiyom, can you draft a short playbook we can attach and offer as an appendix to the DPA? I'll push the certification format to Elena.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Trust & Safety (EMEA)
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 17:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA questions — erasure timing and sunset handback

Karthik / team — draft playbook attached (ERASURE_PLAYBOOK_v1.pdf). High level approach:

1) Termination triggers: customer request, contractual expiry, billing exhaustion, or lawful request. Each trigger maps to a workflow with defined windows.
2) Export window: default 14 days for EU production; shortened to 7 days with signed explicit waiver from customer for non-essential datasets.
3) Backup handling: we classify backups as: a) live object store snapshots (fast recovery), b) incremental write-ahead logs, c) long-term archival snapshots.
   - For a) and b) we will mark tombstones immediately at erasure start and schedule irrecoverable cryptographic destruction within 14 days.
   - For c) (archival) we propose a documented carveout only if the customer has expressly purchased archival retention — otherwise archival snapshots will be scheduled for destruction within 90 days and documented in the certificate.
4) Certification: a signed PDF containing: list of deleted object keys, deletion timestamps (ISO8601), HMAC per object, and the Redwood erasure-job id. We can host the certificate on a secure link for 90 days.

Open items for negotiation:
- Elena's request for a 30-day backup tombstone: ops prefers 14 days default, 30 days as an optional paid tier or regulated exception.
- Wording around "irreversible" — we prefer to state "cryptographic destruction" for clarity.

I attached a synchronization diagram (synchronization-diagram.png) that shows the timing between termination signal, export window, tombstone scheduling, and cryptographic destruction job.

Happy to refine with Elena's legal team.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: ERASURE_PLAYBOOK_v1.pdf, synchronization-diagram.png]

From: Elena Markovic <elena.markovic@aurumanalytics.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@aurumanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 08:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA questions — erasure timing and sunset handback

Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround and the diagram, that helps a lot. A few clarifications from our side after internal review:

- Archival carveout: Aurum does not currently buy Redwood long-term archival as a paid tier; we asked for 30 days on tombstone because our legal team is worried about evidence retention requirements for short-term litigation discovery. If we accept a 14-day default, can Redwood include a signed statement in the certificate that you will keep metadata (not payload) about deletion events for 2 years for audit purposes (index-only, no payload retrieval)?
- Certification hosting: 90 days secure link is workable; procurement requests that the certificate link be downloadable and content-addressed (hash in the DPA).
- Recovery waiver: Aurum won't sign a waiver allowing 7-day forced export for production accounts — they want the 14-day export period preserved.

If Redwood agrees to the metadata retention (index-only) for 2 years and to provide content-addressed certificate links, Aurum will accept 14-day tombstone default (no paid tier) and remove the 30-day absolute requirement.

Can you confirm these two concessions are acceptable operationally?

Best,
Elena

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Markovic <elena.markovic@aurumanalytics.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Nov 2028 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA questions — erasure timing and sunset handback

Elena — thanks, this is actionable. Operational confirmation below: 

1) Metadata retention: Redwood will retain deletion metadata (object id, deletion timestamp, erasure-job id, and non-recoverable-flag) for 24 months as an index-only record; payload (object contents) will not be retained and is irretrievable after cryptographic destruction. We will include a clause in the DPA Appendix stating the limited metadata retention purpose (audit/regulatory inquiries) and access controls for retrieval.

2) Certificate hosting & content address: the erasure certificate will be generated as a signed PDF and stored behind a time-limited secure link. The certificate's SHA-256 hash will be included in the DPA appendix and in the email confirmation. The hosting window will be 90 days; Redwood can provide a certified snapshot of the hash to Aurum's legal team on request after the hosting window ends.

3) Export window: Redwood confirms 14 days export window for EU production accounts; no 7-day forced export without explicit customer acceptance. That will be in the Appendix as the standard flow.

4) Backup tombstone: default 14-day tombstone for live snapshots and incremental logs; archival snapshots (long-term archives) are out of scope unless procured. If Aurum later purchases archival, a separate appendix will define the archival retention and destruction timing.

We'll update the DPA redline to reflect the above and circulate for signature. Laura — please attach the updated appendix and the certificate template before we re-send.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: updated_DPA_appendix_erasure_v2.docx]
